clock_model.rtl_boundary: clk_i rising edge advances one complete normalized E-cycle when clock_enable_i is high
clock_model.historical_boundary: HD63701V0 derives E from its oscillator; E is the documented peripheral and processor cycle reference
clock_model.limitation: Oscillator division, physical multiplexed/non-multiplexed half-cycle waveforms, EPROM programming waveforms, pad delays, setup/hold, and electrical timing are outside this normalized digital boundary

signals.name: clk_i
signals.fact: one rising edge advances one normalized E-cycle

signals.name: clock_enable_i
signals.fact: active-high normalized-cycle enable; low preserves all synchronous digital state

signals.name: reset_n_i
signals.fact: active-low reset; DDR outputs are cleared asynchronously

signals.name: standby_n_i
signals.fact: active-low asynchronous standby boundary; immediately resets active state, suppresses program/external reads and GPIO drive, and preserves RAM plus STBY_PWR while retention power remains valid

signals.name: nmi_n_i
signals.fact: active-low non-maskable interrupt whose falling edge is retained

signals.name: irq1_n_i
signals.fact: active-low maskable interrupt above internal timer and SCI sources

signals.name: standby_power_ok_i
signals.fact: digital integration indication only; it does not model an analog threshold

signals.name: port1_i
signals.fact: physical pin levels returned by PORT1 reads where the mode retains that port

signals.name: port1_o
signals.fact: latched GPIO values or Mode-1 low address byte

signals.name: port1_oe_o
signals.fact: one enables the corresponding output driver

signals.name: port2_i
signals.fact: physical levels for GPIO, timer capture, SCI receive, and mode sampling

signals.name: port2_o
signals.fact: GPIO latch with timer and SCI overrides

signals.name: port2_oe_o
signals.fact: GPIO direction with timer and SCI overrides

signals.name: port3_i
signals.fact: physical or IS3-latched Mode-7 levels; normalized expanded-memory data instead uses external_data_i

signals.name: port3_o
signals.fact: latched Mode-7 GPIO or mode-selected normalized address/data value

signals.name: port3_oe_o
signals.fact: one enables the corresponding output driver

signals.name: port4_i
signals.fact: physical levels returned by PORT4 reads where the mode retains that port

signals.name: port4_o
signals.fact: latched GPIO or mode-selected high/full address byte

signals.name: port4_oe_o
signals.fact: one enables the corresponding output driver

signals.name: is3_n_i
signals.fact: in Mode 7, a falling edge sets the P3CSR flag and optionally captures Port 3

signals.name: os3_n_o
signals.fact: in Mode 7, active-low during the selected Port 3 read or write E-cycle

signals.name: program_address_o
signals.fact: full CPU address for the separately supplied F000-FFFF EPROM image

signals.name: program_read_o
signals.fact: active for read cycles in F000-FFFF in Modes 0/5/6/7, except the initial external Mode-0 reset-vector reads

signals.name: program_data_i
signals.fact: FPGA firmware byte sampled for selected internal EPROM reads

signals.name: external_address_o
signals.fact: normalized full 16-bit address for every external-memory transaction

signals.name: external_data_o
signals.fact: normalized write data; qualified by external_bus_valid_o and external_write_o

signals.name: external_write_o
signals.fact: one denotes a normalized external write

signals.name: external_bus_valid_o
signals.fact: qualifies the normalized external transaction and is always low in Mode 7 and standby

signals.name: external_opcode_fetch_o
signals.fact: qualifies opcode reads on the normalized external bus

signals.name: external_data_i
signals.fact: byte sampled on a completing normalized external read

signals.name: sci_tx_o
signals.fact: normalized asynchronous transmit level

signals.name: sci_clock_o
signals.fact: normalized internal serial clock level

signals.name: timer_irq_o
signals.fact: diagnostic enabled timer request

signals.name: sci_irq_o
signals.fact: diagnostic enabled SCI request

halt_interrupt_behavior: HD63701V0 has no HALT input; SLP retains CPU state while peripherals run, an enabled request vectors, and a masked request resumes at the following instruction; asynchronous STBY instead enters reset-state operation and requires a mode-selected reset-vector restart on release

locators: HD63701V0 sections 2.1-2.4, 2.7, and 2.9-2.13, printed pages 252-269 and 281-292
